Their maximum allowable pressures are: E-2-1, 10.3 barg (ASME) or 16.0 barg (PED) for frame FG; BV-2-1, no single number — ASME B16.34 pressure/temperature chart, e.g. 19.8 bar (Group 1.2 Cl150) or 51.8 bar (Group 1.2 Cl300) at −30 °C, lower of body/seat rating applies; GV-2-1, 6 bar (gauge), PN6, valid up to 40 °C; P-2-1, 250 psi max operating pressure (266 psi max casing pressure) at up to 100 °F; GV-2-2, 6 bar (gauge), PN6; FV-2-1, no single number — limited by body pressure class (PN16 to PN100 / CL150 to CL600 per ASME B16.34) and packing limits; P-2-2, 250 psi (266 psi casing) at up to 100 °F; PV-2-2, no single number — body class PN16 to PN100 / CL150 to CL600 per ASME B16.34; P-2-3, 250 psi (266 psi casing) at up to 100 °F; GV-2-5, 6 bar (gauge), PN6; P-3-1, 250 psi (266 psi casing) at up to 100 °F; BV-3-1, no single number — same ASME B16.34 chart as BV-2-1; P-3-2, 250 psi (266 psi casing) at up to 100 °F. final.answer: The valve operated by TIC-27-2 is TV-27-2, and the item directly upstream of BV-24-1 is heat exchanger E-24-1. E-24-1's datasheet gives a maximum design temperature of 177 °C (350 °F) under the ASME code (180 °C / 356 °F under PED). TV-27-2's datasheet does not state which seat material this specific valve has, so its fluid-temperature limit cannot be pinned to one value: it ranges from 80 °C (180 °F) for Delrin seats and 90 °C (200 °F) for UHMWPE seats, up to 230–260 °C for PTFE/Polyfill seats and 315 °C (600 °F) for PEEK or metal seats. Therefore, which of the two has the lowest maximum fluid temperature depends on TV-27-2's seat material: with Delrin or UHMWPE seats the valve (80–90 °C) is lower than the exchanger (177 °C), but with any other seat material the exchanger (177 °C) is the lower of the two.

The datasheet does not give one single maximum pressure number — the allowable pressure depends on temperature, the body material group and pressure class, and the seat material.
